derived_observations: In all 10 cases, self already held six MELON seeds at Day4 hour10 and had at least one empty unlocked tile.
Using actual hourly unit positions from deterministic replay, an empty unlocked tile was at most two public MOVE actions from the nearest self unit in every case.
Therefore a Day4 MELON productive-State entry required at most three unit actions (MOVE <=2 plus PLANT) from the observed Day4 hour10 State, with 14 action turns remaining in the day.
A Day4 MELON origin maps by public rules to a Day10 production opportunity and Day14 harvest eligibility.
Thus absence of any feasible next-cycle-production-positioned G1 entry is rejected as an explanation for self's Day8 time placement.

This does not show that choosing MELON would improve terminal self, nor that MELON is an optimal asset. It only establishes that at least one next-cycle-production-positioned G1 State-entry was physically available.

Because a feasible entry existed but was not realized in the observed self State, the next unresolved layer is the projection from feasible entries to actual unit/action allocation, not upstream resource impossibility.
boundary: No Candidate, Direction, or policy mutation is introduced.
The replay was required only because prior raw logs omitted hourly unit positions.
Existing MELON seed path requires no market purchase.
Entry feasibility is not equivalent to eventual production, realization, or terminal benefit; later crop survival/care actions remain separate.
